newsitem.title: NEPAL: Germanys' Noell wins bid for Nepal power plant.
newsitem.headline: Germanys' Noell wins bid for Nepal power plant.

text.p: Germany's Noell Stahl-und Machinenbau GmbH has won a 1.21 billion rupee ($21.3 million) contract to supply steel equipment for a hydroelectric plant in Nepal, officials said on Sunday.

They said Noell offered the lowest bid among 13 competitors from eight nations in a race to supply equipment for the 144-megawatt Kali Gandaki hydroelectric plant in the Syangja district of western Nepal.
The state-owned Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) said in a statement that the tender amount quoted by the German firm was 20.86 percent less than estimates for the work.
"The plant is expected to go on trial production in 2000," said Kriti Chand Thakur, NEA Managing Director.

The Manila-based Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the Japanese government are funding $160 million each for the project which is expected to cost $425 million. The Nepali government will raise the remaing amount from internal sources.
Noell has also undertaken the construction of a part of the Marsyangdi powerhouse, another hydroelectric facility in central Nepal completed with German aid.
In the Kali Gandaki project, Italy's Impregilo Spa is building the civil works while Japan's Toshiba group will supply turbines and generators.
One of the world's poorest countries, Nepal is rich in river water resources. The overall hydroelectric potential is estimated at 83,000 megawatts.
The kingdom uses less than 0.5 percent of this as only 15 percent of its 22 million people have access to electricity.
